findings.evidence: `exists_tendsto_of_subsingleton` requires `IsCompact K`, `MapsTo f U K`, and `w ∈ closure U`; only `clusterSetOn_eq_singleton_of_tendsto` proves the unconditional limit-to-singleton direction.
findings.fix: Qualify the converse with the compact-image and closure-point hypotheses of `exists_tendsto_of_subsingleton`, and avoid describing it as an unconditional equivalence.
findings.issue: Lines 17–19 and 62–63 claim that a singleton cluster set is equivalent to having a limit; the converse is false without relative compactness, since values may have one finite cluster point while other subnet values escape to infinity.

findings.evidence: `exists_continuousOn_closure_eqOn` concludes only existence of a continuous extension at lines 293–296, while `injOn_closure_of_injOn_frontier` explicitly assumes `InjOn F (frontier U)` at lines 312–320.
findings.fix: Say singleton cluster sets produce the continuous extension, while a homeomorphism additionally requires proving boundary injectivity (or an equivalent inverse-extension argument).
findings.issue: Lines 40–46 and 283–286 say singleton boundary cluster sets yield a homeomorphism, but the extension theorem yields only `ContinuousOn` and `EqOn`; frontier injectivity is a separate, unproved hypothesis.

summary: The module documentation overstates what singleton cluster sets establish, omitting compactness and injectivity hypotheses required by the actual results.
